messages:
maria: Heads up — after last night's kernel+driver push to eu-west the Ampere racks are showing partial P2P disable. Not full outage but NCCL collectives degrade on some jobs. Any immediate eyes?
aj: seeing the same. Canary jobs in rack-7 losing peer access between GPUs 0<->1 on a subset of hosts. Other hosts in the same rack look fine.
devon: can you paste the dmesg / nvidia-smi topo output from an affected host?
maria: pasted below from host amp-rack7-12: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: peer access denied by kernel (BAR1 mismatch?)
[ 1234.567915] nvidia: p2p: PCIe ACS for device 0000:3b:00.0 is set, disallowing peer access
```
maria: and `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows `NVL NVL XG LINK` inconsistent with other hosts.
kevin: hmm, we rolled kernel 6.2.15 + driver 535.86 across eu-west canaries last night. Ampere boxes on older BIOSes might have BAR1 windows sized smaller, driver is now stricter about PCIe ACS.
aj: quick check: `cat /sys/module/nvidia_peermem/parameters/peer_access_enabled` returns `0` on affected hosts. On healthy hosts it's `1`.
devon: is this the ACS/PCIe ACS isolation causing BAR1 fallback? If ACS bit set, driver refuses p2p unless we override. We saw this with the 525 -> 535 lineage in staging but not this pattern (intermittent per-host).
ops-jun: I just triggered a canary rollback to driver 528 on two hosts in rack-7. Job throughput jumped ~1.8x immediately. Reverting looks promising.
sre-bot: deploy event: driver-rollback initiated by ops-jun on amp-rack7-12 and amp-rack7-13 at 2026-03-18T03:12Z :arrow_double_down: 
maria: good signal. But we need a long-term fix because many EU racks are on slightly different PCIe root port configs. Two options: 1) pin to older driver until we CVE-check and kernel+driver reconcile; 2) allow driver to use `pcie_acs_override=downstream` kernel cmdline on affected hosts (risky for isolation).
kevin: +1 we should avoid global `pcie_acs_override` unless we can limit to the problematic hosts. Also we need to check BAR1 sizing: `lspci -vvv` shows `Region 0: BAR1 64-bit` size mismatches on ~6 hosts. That can explain the "BAR1 mismatch" message.
devon: can we script detection? Something like: ```bash
for h in $(cat eu-west-ampere-hosts); do ssh $h "lspci -s 3b:00 -vvv | grep 'Region 1:' || true"; done
```
aj: I'll run a scan across eu-west and flag hosts with `peer_access_enabled=0` and BAR1 size < expected.
ops-jun: note for temporary mitigation we can add a host-level driver config: `NVreg_RestrictPCI:0` and `NVreg_EnablePCIePeerAccess:1` in modprobe.d — need testing. Not sure if that interacts with ACS.
kevin: also check NCCL logs — we got repeated `NCCL WARN` about `p2p disabled` and fallback to `ring` which explains throughput drop and increased CPU overhead.
maria: cost implication: fallback increases CPU and host memory usage and prolongs jobs by ~30-40% on some RL training runs. For active customers in eu-west this could blow committed capacity. We should prioritize.
devon: proposal: 1) Run the host scan and create a list of impacted hosts. 2) For critical hosts, rollback driver to 528 as short-term. 3) In parallel, coordinate with kernel team to avoid ACS strictness in next kernel patch or test `pcie_acs_override` on canaries with isolation tests. 4) Work with BIOS team to standardize BAR1 sizing during hw maintenance.
aj: started the scan — ETA ~20m. I'll post results here.
kevin: I'll open an infra-ticket with inventory of BIOS versions, BAR1 sizes, and which hosts got the 535 rollouts. Link it here when created.
maria: also pinging @platform-qa — we need a new regression test that ensures driver+kernel combos don't disable P2P for Ampere.
ops-jun: noted. Also we should add a console dashboard alert: `nvidia_peer_access_count < expected` per-rack so SREs can detect earlier.
sre-bot: alert: eu-west ampere p2p anomaly rate spiked from 0.2% to 8.7% in last 30m — ticket created INFRA-1248.
aj: scan done — 6 hosts impacted: amp-rack7-12, -13, -21, amp-rack9-03, -04, amp-rack9-07. I'll paste the output in a follow-up message.
maria: thanks. For the short term I'll approve rollback for the 6 hosts. After rollback we'll run load tests to validate. If rollback helps, schedule a slow re-roll with BIOS+kernel changes verified.
kevin: filed INFRA-1248 with initial findings and rollback plan. CC: hw-bios, kernel-team.
devon: long-term, I'd prefer we automate a compatibility matrix check in ci: driver version vs kernel vs BIOS vs NCCL baseline. We keep hitting these multi-factor regressions.
maria: agreed. For now rollback in progress. Will update after post-rollback perf check. :thumbsup:
